activities.caption: pair each term with what it names
activities.name: gnVocabMatch

config.prompt: Examiners and geneticists both lean on these — pair them:

pairs.right: a gene's location on a chromosome
alternative versions of the same gene at the same locus
two identical alleles at a locus
two different alleles — one may mask the other

config.why: Two tall plants — TT and Tt — share a phenotype while carrying different genotypes; only breeding tests can tell them apart.

config.prompt: PMAT — put the stages in order:
items: Metaphase — chromatids align at the equator
Anaphase — sister chromatids separate to opposite poles
config.why: The choreography is the physical guarantee of the genetic result: equal, exact shares — mistakes in around 1 in 10¹⁰ bases after proofreading and repair.

activities.anchor: Two layers of shuffling make every gamete
activities.caption: true or false — the two shuffles
activities.name: gnShuffleJudge

statements.s: In crossing over, homologous chromosomes physically swap segments while paired up.
statements.why: One to three crossovers per chromosome on average.

statements.s: Independent assortment happens because each homologous pair lines up at the equator independently of the others.
statements.why: That alone gives 2²³ ≈ 8.4 million genetically different gametes.

statements.s: Crossing over happens in meiosis II.
statements.why: It happens in meiosis I, while the homologues are paired up; meiosis II separates sister chromatids, mitosis-style.

statements.s: Fertilisation multiplies the 8.4 million by another 8.4 million — which is why no two people (except identical twins) share a genome.

activities.anchor: Family tree (pedigree) analysis reads these patterns backwards
activities.caption: file the pedigree clues by inheritance pattern
activities.name: gnPedigreeBuckets

config.prompt: Three patterns, six clues — file each:

items.label: cystic fibrosis — two carrier parents, 1-in-4 per child
polydactyly — extra fingers in every generation
sickle-cell — carriers malaria-resistant, so the allele persists
affected fathers passing it to all daughters but no sons

config.why: Recessive hides in carriers and skips; dominant shows every generation yet can stay rare; X-linked follows the criss-cross.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — beyond dominant and recessive
activities.name: gnCoCloze

config.text: Red × white snapdragons give %%0%% offspring — the heterozygote is a genuine blend, and the 1:2:1 genotype ratio becomes visible in the phenotype. In codominance both alleles express fully at once: AB blood carries %%1%% antigens, and the Iᴮ allele is codominant with Iᴬ but both dominant over %%2%% — type %%3%%.
config.hint: Six genotypes, four phenotypes — and O-negative donors are universal but can receive only from O.

activities.anchor: Fathers pass their X only to daughters
activities.caption: the criss-cross — drag from sons to daughters
activities.name: gnCrissCompare

config.prompt: A colour-blind father — drag the divider across his children:

before.label: his sons
before.text: They receive his Y and a fresh X from their mother — they escape unless SHE is a carrier.

after.label: his daughters
after.text: They must at least carry the allele — the X^c passes down; the criss-cross pattern.

config.why: The X is large and gene-rich, the Y small — so males express whatever their single X carries: about 1 in 12 men is red–green colour blind, versus about 1 in 200 women.

activities.anchor: Genes on the same chromosome are
activities.caption: map the pair — run the linkage decision
activities.name: gnLinkageBranch

config.root: Two genes, two phenotypes, thousands of counted offspring — where do they sit?

choices.label: Different chromosomes
choices.feedback: They assort independently — the 9:3:3:1 dihybrid ratio.

choices.label: Same chromosome, far apart
choices.feedback: Crossing over falls between them often.

indep.text: Mendel's seed colour and shape sat on different chromosomes — which is why his ratios came out clean.

far.text: The further apart two genes are, the more often recombination separates them — measurable as recombination frequency.

close.text: Inherited together: linkage — and Sturtevant's 1913 map was built from exactly these counted frequencies.

config.why: Linkage analysis became the first method of mapping gene positions, decades before anyone could read DNA — and it convinced the sceptics that chromosomes carry heredity.

activities.anchor: populations form smooth bell curves instead of 3:1 ratios
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the polygenic answer
activities.name: gnPolySpot

config.prompt: This complex-traits answer contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: Height, skin colour, blood pressure and diabetes risk are shaped by thousands of genes plus environment.
Each gene contributes a little, so populations form smooth bell curves instead of 3:1 ratios.
Identical twins reared apart still differ in height by a few centimetres.
Most human traits follow clean 3:1 ratios once you count enough offspring.
Simple Mendelian cases are the exceptions that taught the rules.
config.correction: Clean 3:1 ratios are the EXCEPTION — most human traits are polygenic, with environment setting the final value.
config.why: The ratio arithmetic remains the foundation on which the messy multigene reality is understood — the Punnett square is the atom the complexity is assembled from.
